display.purpose: The hero headline on white, Ink with one Crimson word, max 11ch. The page's one bold element.

hero-sub.purpose: The one-line sub under the display, Soft Ink, max 60ch.

headline.purpose: Section titles on white, max 20ch. No eyebrow above.

headline-sm.purpose: A secondary statement inside a section, max 16ch.

title.purpose: Step names in the steps list.

title-sm.purpose: Before/after column heads and the wordmark.

lede.purpose: One line under each section headline; install steps.

button.purpose: The crimson primary button label, white.

tag.purpose: Bordered honesty labels such as Example, beside a heading.

mono-line.purpose: Quoted prompts and 'Then say start here'.

mono-number.purpose: Step numbers, list counters, tabular star counts.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Every state transition and the hero fade-up.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Button, chip and start-here bar colour/border transitions; button arrow nudge (4px right).

motion.name: hero-fade-up
motion.purpose: The one load animation, on hero headline, sub and actions. Off under reduced motion.

motion.name: copied-hold
motion.purpose: How long a chip or the start-here bar shows its Copied state.

narrative.overview:
Frontier is a clean white page held inside one 1200px column with hairline side rules. Sections are split by full-width hairlines, never boxed into cards, and side-by-side content sits in uneven splits. The page reads like a well-kept notebook: ruled, numbered, quiet.

The one bold element is the display headline at the top: Inter 800, tightly tracked, set in Ink on white, with its last word in Crimson. Everything after it stays restrained. Crimson appears on white as a signal: the one filled primary button, step and list numbers, the good path in the before/after, the copied state and the focus ring. Fira Code appears only where the reader is looking at something they type or count.

The system is flat. No gradients, no grain, no shadows, no glows. Structure comes from 1px Hairline rules and white space; depth is not simulated.
keyCharacteristics: White page everywhere; a 1200px column with hairline side rules.
Sections divided by full-width hairlines; content never sits in cards.
One bold element per view: the display headline, with one word in Crimson.
Inter for all words; Fira Code only for commands, numbers, quoted prompts and the start-here bar.
Crimson as a signal on white; the primary button is its only solid fill.
Flat surfaces: no box-shadow, no gradients; light theme only.
Motion limited to one hero fade-up, the copy state and short hover transitions.

rules.name: The Crimson Signal Rule
rules.body: On white, crimson marks things to act on or follow: the primary button, one word of the headline, numbers, the good path, the copied state, the start-here bar, focus. The primary button is the only solid crimson block; nothing else gets a crimson fill.

rules.name: The No Gradient Rule
rules.body: No purple-to-blue gradients, no blue or violet anywhere in the system, and no gradients at all on this page.

rules.name: The Light Only Rule
rules.body: Light theme only (`color-scheme: light`). No dark mode, no theme switch.

rules.name: The Mono Means Command Rule
rules.body: Fira Code is used only for commands, step and list numbers, numeric table values, quoted prompts, "Then say start here" and the start-here bar. Headlines, body, labels, tags and nav are always Inter.

rules.name: The Bare Headline Rule
rules.body: Headlines stand alone. No eyebrow or kicker line above a headline; a lede sits below it instead. A tag may sit beside a heading on its baseline, never above it.

rules.name: The Plain Words Rule
rules.body: No hype in any UI text: never revolutionize, seamless, empower, elevate, unleash, robust, supercharge, next-gen, game-changer, or "unlock your potential". Lead with the mechanism and a number.

rules.name: The 4px Grid Rule
rules.body: Every padding, margin and gap is a multiple of 4px (observed scale: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 96, 112, 128). No arbitrary values.

rules.name: The Ruled Frame Rule
rules.body: Structure is drawn with 1px Hairline rules: column edges, section tops, column dividers, list and table rows. Content never sits in cards.

rules.name: The Uneven Split Rule
rules.body: Side-by-side content uses unequal spans (5/7, 4/6). No rows of three equal cards, ever.

rules.name: The One Bold Element Rule
rules.body: Each view has exactly one statement element; on this page it is the display headline. Section headlines below it stay in Ink at headline scale, and nothing else gets display treatment.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: No shadows, no glows, no floating cards. If something needs separating, give it a hairline rule.

dos: Do keep the page white inside the 1200px ruled frame, with the display headline as the one bold element.
Do separate sections and list rows with 1px Hairline rules and divide columns with a vertical rule.
Do split side-by-side content unevenly (5fr / 7fr, or 48px / 4fr / 6fr).
Do keep every padding, margin and gap on the 4px grid.
Do use Fira Code for anything the reader types or counts, and Inter for everything else.
Do use crimson on white only as a signal: the primary button, one headline word, numbers, the good path, copied state, focus, the start-here bar.
Do make every command a tap-to-copy chip with a visible Copied state.
Do turn off the hero fade-up and smooth scrolling under reduced motion.
donts: Don't use purple-to-blue gradients, any gradient, or any blue or violet.
Don't add glows (blurred colour halos behind buttons or text) or any box-shadow, floating or offset.
Don't put content in cards, and never set three equal cards in a row.
Don't add a second bold element; section headlines stay in Ink at headline scale.
Don't put an eyebrow or kicker above a headline.
Don't set headlines, labels or tags in Fira Code.
Don't give anything but the primary button a solid crimson fill.
Don't add a dark theme or a theme switch.
Don't write revolutionize, seamless, empower, elevate, unleash, robust, supercharge, next-gen, game-changer or "unlock your potential" in any UI text.
